boundaries: Interaction format is separate from the knowledge target and cognitive operation.

Generator uses public contracts and course inputs; private evaluator prompts, labels and holdouts are outside this catalog.

categories.label: Entity A: what the source shows

formats.teacher_key: Every entry maps to one or more defensible category IDs; if a single key is required, overlapping categories must be resolved.
conditions: Categories express a declared knowledge distinction, not decorative bins.
Entity and semantic relation remain explicit when flattening the two-dimensional native key.
Only source-supported descriptions enter the bank; supply evidence for each classification.
Do not claim independent inference after labels or feedback have supplied the distinction.
quality_risks: Ambiguous descriptions fit several people or relations.
Slot counts, color, order or elimination let learners solve without knowing the content.
Hardcoded is/seems/wanted relations become invalid outside character analysis.

formats.cognitive_operation: Choose the supported claim among genuinely competing interpretations or applications.
formats.teacher_key: One defensible keyed option; each distractor has a named misconception and source-based rejection reason.
conditions: Use recognition only where recognition assesses the target.
Give all options comparable linguistic specificity and avoid positional/length cues.
Judge whether multiple options are defensible using the complete visible source.
Treat answer-position distribution as a sequence diagnostic, not universal item truth.
quality_risks: Invented implausible distractors make a trivial question.
The stem repeats only key wording.
Feedback previews a later independent answer.

formats.cognitive_operation: Select source evidence relevant to a specific claim and distinguish merely related text.
required_payload: claim or an unambiguous claim in the prompt
formats.teacher_key: An explicit set of relevant evidence choices with a claim-to-evidence warrant; multiple defensible selections are allowed when the task does not ask for one best.
conditions: All evidence options are exact text visible to the learner, or their paraphrase status is explicit.
Ask for one best only if a defensible comparison criterion exists.
A line containing a topic word is not necessarily evidence.
Follow selection with learner-produced explanation when the target includes reasoning.
quality_risks: Only one quotation is offered.
Correct lines are pre-highlighted for an independent check.
The text is hidden while a quote is required.
Selected evidence is counted as reasoning without an explanation.

formats.cognitive_operation: Produce a short reason that links source evidence to a declared interpretation.

formats.teacher_key: Atomic rubric requirements specify the claim, evidence and warrant needed; accept alternative wording and evidence consistent with the source.
conditions: The explanation is not already written in the prompt or starter.
Learner can see all source material required by the rubric.
Rubric tests meaning, not only keywords or minimum words.
Separate quote accuracy from semantic support.
quality_risks: Minimum word count masquerades as reasoning.
Repeating the prompt or copying a quote passes.
Rubric demands terminology or facts the lesson never taught.

conditions: Question formation serves the lesson target, not only character roleplay.

formats.cognitive_operation: Evaluate a stated defense against source evidence and explain whether it holds.

payload_sketch.support: The counterpart claim and all source evidence needed to test it.

formats.teacher_key: Accept support, rejection or qualification where defensible; rubric distinguishes a verdict from its evidential reason.
conditions: Counterpart claim is explicit and frozen in the packet.
The source supplies enough evidence to test the claim.
Scoring accepts justified alternative positions where the text permits them.
Any scripted counterpart speech is marked as authored, not presented as a source quotation.
quality_risks: The generator invents an excuse then treats it as a textual fact.
The question embeds its desired rebuttal.
A one-sided rubric rejects justified disagreement.
